Verify the redacted PDFs at /root/redacted/paper{1,2,3}.pdf by checking:

1. That all identifying information has been removed
2. That the paper content is still intact

Run this Python code:

```python
import fitz

for i in range(1, 4):
    doc = fitz.open(f"/root/redacted/paper{i}.pdf")
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"=== Redacted Paper {i} ===")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    
    # Check metadata
    print(f"\nMetadata: {doc.metadata}")
    
    # Check first page text
    page = doc[0]
    text = page.get_text()
    print(f"\n--- Page 1 text (first 2000 chars) ---")
    print(text[:2000])
    
    # Search for things that should be gone
    full_text = ""
    for p in doc:
        full_text += p.get_text()
    
    # Check for author names
    author_names = {
        1: ["Yueqian Lin", "Zhengmian Hu", "Qinsi Wang", "Hengfan Zhang", 
            "Jayakumar Subramanian", "Nikos Vlassis", "Hai Helen", "Yiran Chen",
            "yueqian.lin@duke.edu", "zhengmianh@adobe.com", "Duke University",
            "Adobe", "arXiv:2509", "linyueqian", "Preprint"],
        2: ["Jiatong Shi", "Xinyi Bai", "Keyi Zhang", "Yuning Wu",
            "Yuxun Tang", "Yifeng Yu", "Qin Jin", "Shinji Watanabe",
            "jiatongs@cs.cmu.edu", "Carnegie Mellon", "Duke Kunshan", 
            "Cornell University", "Renmin University", "Georgia Institute",
            "Interspeech 2024", "Kos, Greece", "10.21437", 
            "Shengyuan Xu", "Pengcheng Zhu", "kan-bayashi",
            "1880", "1881", "1882", "1883", "1884"],
        3: ["Yueqian Lin", "Yuzhe Fu", "Jingyang Zhang", "Yudong Liu",
            "Jianyi Zhang", "Jingwei Sun", "Hai Li", "Yiran Chen",
            "yl768@duke.edu", "Duke University", 
            "NSF 2112562", "ARO W911NF", "ICML Workshop"],
    }
    
    print(f"\n--- Checking for remaining identifiers ---")
    found_issues = False
    for term in author_names[i]:
        if term in full_text:
            # Find which page it's on
            for pn, p in enumerate(doc):
                if term in p.get_text():
                    print(f"  WARNING: '{term}' still found on page {pn+1}")
                    # Print context
                    idx = p.get_text().find(term)
                    context = p.get_text()[max(0,idx-50):idx+len(term)+50]
                    print(f"    Context: ...{context}...")
                    found_issues = True
    
    if not found_issues:
        print("  All identifiers successfully redacted!")
    
    # Check that content is still present (e.g., abstract, section headings)
    print(f"\n--- Checking content preservation ---")
    page1 = doc[0].get_text()
    if "Abstract" in full_text or "abstract" in full_text or "ABSTRACT" in full_text:
        print("  Abstract: Present")
    else:
        print("  WARNING: Abstract may be missing!")
    
    # Check page count
    print(f"  Total pages: {len(doc)}")
    
    doc.close()
```

ABSTRACT
We present Voice Evaluation of Reasoning Ability (VERA), a benchmark for
evaluating reasoning ability in voice-interactive systems under real-time conver-
sational constraints. VERA comprises 2,931 voice-native episodes derived from
established text benchmarks and organized into five tracks (Math, Web, Science,
Long-Context, Factual). Each item is adapted for speech interaction while pre-
serving reasoning difficulty. VERA enables direct text–voice comparison within
model families and supports analysis of how architectural choices affect reliability.
We assess 12 contemporary voice systems alongside strong text baselines and
observe large, consistent modality gaps: on competition mathematics a leading text
model attains 74.8% accuracy while its voice counterpart reaches 6.1%; macro-
averaged across tracks the best text models achieve 54.0% versus 11.3% for voice.
Latency–accuracy analyses reveal a low-latency plateau, where fast voice sys-
tems cluster around ∼10% accuracy, while approaching text performance requires
sacrificing real-time interaction. Diagnostic experiments indicate that common
mitigations are insufficient. Increasing “thinking time” yields negligible gains; a
decoupled cascade that separates reasoning from narration improves accuracy but
still falls well short of text and introduces characteristic grounding/consistency
errors. Failure analyses further show distinct error signatures across native stream-
ing, end-to-end, and cascade designs. VERA provides a reproducible testbed
and targeted diagnostics for architectures that decouple thinking from speaking,
offering a principled way to measure progress toward real-time voice assistants
that are both fluent and reliably reasoned.
